mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 1.5%, market expectations for future rate cuts diminish, lowering real discount rates and increasing present-value weights on longer-term equity cash flows, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day rolling mean during the high-rate period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in labor market participation (HOUST) signals a weakening labor market, prompting risk-aversion compression and a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month while HOUST decreases by >5% month-over-month
failure_condition: During such trigger events, SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months predicts strengthening aggregate demand, which elevates equity risk premia and produces a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite INDPRO growth above threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5% for two consecutive months in a period of tight labor (PAYEMS < 150K), supply-side pressures dominate, depressing equity valuations and generating a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 2.5 for two consecutive months AND PAYEMS < 150K
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns during such episodes are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% triggers expectations of monetary tightening, which increases real risk-free rates and compresses equity discounting, producing a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the tightening onset (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (not directly observable in the given catalog, but proxy via GDPC1 > 2% above trend) predict optimism about future consumption, which elevates equity valuations and yields a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 above 2% trend for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during acceleration (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in consumer confidence (not directly observable; proxy via HOUST falling by >15% in a month) combined with rising job openings (not directly observable; proxy via RSAFS > 500K) signals labor market dislocation, which increases uncertainty and produces a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by >15% in a month AND RSAFS > 500K
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the supply-side inflation gap (CPIAUCSL - INDPRO) exceeds 1.5% for two consecutive months in a low-unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4%), it indicates persistent supply pressures that erode equity value, resulting in a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL - INDPRO > 1.5 for two consecutive months AND UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns during such episodes are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
